title: Definition by transfinite recursion on a well-ordered set
statement: Let $(E,\le)$ be a well-ordered set (a total order in which every nonempty subset has a least element) and let $\mathcal V$ be a collection of objects (a set, or a class such as the class of all tuples consisting of a commutative ring and ring maps). Suppose that for every $x\in E$ a rule $G_x$ is given which assigns to every family $(v_y)_{y<x}$ of members of $\mathcal V$ indexed by $\{y\in E:y<x\}$ a member $G_x\big((v_y)_{y<x}\big)$ of $\mathcal V$. Then there is a family $(v_x)_{x\in E}$ of members of $\mathcal V$ such that $v_x=G_x\big((v_y)_{y<x}\big)$ for every $x\in E$, and it is unique.
